cards.text: Picture it, friend. The exiles are back from captivity, Cyrus king of Persia has authorized the cedar logs they're bringing in (Ezra 3:7), and the foundation of the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem is laid (Ezra 3:10-11). Then the enemies of Judah and Benjamin hear that the exiles are building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel.

So they walk right up to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah (Haggai 1:1), and the heads of the families. They say they seek Israel's God just like the exiles do, and they've been sacrificing to Him since King Esar-haddon of Assyria brought them there.

cards.question: The enemies of Judah and Benjamin tell Zerubbabel they seek the same God he does. So what do they offer him?

answers.text: To pay for the cedar logs

cards.text: Zerubbabel, Jeshua the priest (Ezra 3:2) and the other heads of the families hear them out. Then it's their turn to answer.

cards.question: True or false: Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the family heads welcome the offer from the enemies of Judah and Benjamin to help build.
Zerubbabel and the family heads say they alone must build the house for the LORD, as King ___ commanded them.

cards.text: The people of the land just heard no. Some folks hear no and go home, but these folks change their whole approach.

cards.question: After hearing no, the people of the land change their approach. What do they set out to do to the people of Judah?

answers.text: Tax them for using the land

cards.text: Then they hire counselors against Judah to frustrate their plans. That's like paying somebody a FULL salary just to walk in every morning and unplug my oven.

cards.question: The counselors hired against Judah keep frustrating their plans from the reign of Cyrus all the way down to the reign of which king?

cards.text: At the beginning of the reign of Xerxes, king of Persia, an accusation is lodged against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.

Then in the days of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel and the rest of his associates write him a letter, written in Aramaic and then translated. Friend, these folks are NOT playing.

cards.question: Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe write a letter to King Artaxerxes. What city is it against?

cards.text: Rehum and Shimshai's letter opens with a LONG list of who it's from: judges, officials, the Elamites of Susa, and the peoples the great and honorable Ashurbanipal deported and settled in Samaria and elsewhere west of the Euphrates, all signing as the king's servants. That's the birthday card at work where the whole office signs and nobody can find room to write.
Then the letter gets to the point. It tells the king the Jews who came from him have returned to Jerusalem and are rebuilding it, restoring its walls and repairing its foundations.

cards.question: In their letter to King Artaxerxes, Rehum and Shimshai call Jerusalem that ___ and wicked city.
Next the letter warns the king about what happens if Jerusalem is rebuilt. What do Rehum and Shimshai say the Jews will stop paying?

cards.text: They say they're writing because they serve the palace and it's not fitting for them to let the king be dishonored. That's the coworker who CCs your boss on everything and signs off, "Just looking out for the team!"

cards.question: Rehum and Shimshai want the king to believe Jerusalem has always been trouble. How do they say he can check?
Rehum and Shimshai end their letter with a warning: if Jerusalem is rebuilt and its walls restored, King Artaxerxes will have no ___ west of the Euphrates.

cards.text: King Artaxerxes writes back and says their letter was translated and read in his presence. Somebody sat and read that letter to a king, friend, and I can't get anybody to read a recipe card past the word "preheat."

cards.question: King Artaxerxes issues a decree and a search is made. What does it turn up about Jerusalem?

answers.text: It revolted against kings long ago
It had never been ruled by kings
It had always lived in peace

cards.question: True or false: King Artaxerxes also says mighty kings once ruled over Jerusalem and were paid tribute.
King Artaxerxes orders Rehum and Shimshai to make the men rebuilding Jerusalem ___.
True or false: King Artaxerxes says Jerusalem can never be rebuilt, no matter what.

cards.text: Then the king tells them not to neglect this matter. That's the boss who ends every email with "Let's not drop the ball on this."

cards.question: King Artaxerxes's letter is read to Rehum, Shimshai and their associates. What do they do?

answers.text: Go to Jerusalem and stop the work by force
Wait a whole year and then send word
Write the king back asking for details

cards.text: Then the Bible says, "Thus the construction of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased, and it remained at a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia." But keep that apron on, friend, because this story is NOT done.
